memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Conviction medium on the park, a working hypothesis on the Q4 2026 mobile service revenue turn. The framework's park rule is triggered on trackability ('Leading indicators' at D, quarterly series only) and the record does not argue against it, because the case fails the 20 percent bar on its return before it fails on tracking. Two ways back in are named: first, a Q4 2026 print with Finnish mobile service revenue growth at +1.5 percent or better year on year, FY2026 comparable EBITDA at EUR 830 million or better with non-comparable adjustments under EUR 10 million, and a price at or below EUR 31 to 33, at which the modal path clears or nearly clears the bar; second, at any price near today's EUR 36.46, evidence for the cleared branch (two quarters of consumer postpaid ARPU above EUR 24.50 and software organic growth above 8 percent with positive segment EBITDA), which would move the 'Investment Thesis' to C and the odds on the re-rating to even. The first hard evidence arrives with the Q3 2026 results on 21-Oct-26 and then the Q4 2026 print.
case: - What kind of case: a cause-for-concern case in a high-quality, low-growth business, not a change case. Elisa has lost its growth premium (five-year median 24-month-forward P/E 17.27x to 14.47x) because a late-2025 domestic price war put mobile service revenue into decline and the software growth engine stalled, forcing two component guidance cuts on 15-Jul-26.

- The change is internal, dated and defensive: a new chief executive and finance director, a EUR 40 million cost programme delivered on schedule (357 job cuts in Q4 2025), campaign price rises of about EUR 10 in early 2026 that DNA followed and Telia moderately, a software division under new leadership from 30-Mar-26, and a mechanical roll-off of 12-month discounted contracts due in Q4 2026. The framework's screen rule (three strong internal forces, or a chief-executive change plus a guidance rise) is failed: two forces strong, guidance cut.

- The external field is against: five of seven forces are headwinds; the speed-tier tailwind is fading (5G penetration growth 9 percent in 2025 against 12 percent in 2024; 58 percent already on high-speed plans); Finnish GDP about +1 percent in 2026; European CIO IT budgets growing 1.8 percent; rates re-priced yield proxies in spring 2026.
counter_case: - At the 'Investment Thesis': Q2 2026 is an artificial trough made by the mechanical lag of 12-month discounted contracts signed in the H2 2025 price war, so the recovery is arithmetic. Front-book prices are already above prior year, churn is at its ten-year Q2 average of 16.7 percent, DNA followed the EUR 10 rise, Telia co-operated and says it has stopped accepting share loss. When the contracts expire in Q4 2026 the back book re-prices, mobile service revenue turns to +1 percent or more, the EUR 40 million programme reaches full run-rate, the software backlog converts, FY2026 comparable EBITDA beats the EUR 830 million midpoint, the sell-side upgrades, and the multiple recovers to its two-year median of 16.25x (a 12 percent re-rating) or further. Conceded: the lag is mechanical, the indicators are in place, the turn is probable at six in ten. Held at D because the sell-side already assumes the turn (about +1 percent telecom service revenue; FY2027 earnings per share +2.9 percent), so a turn that happens brings no upgrade and a re-rating needs a turn that beats; because even the cleared branch is at the bar only with both the higher multiple and the higher earnings, at three-in-ten odds; and because software is not lagged but broken and the dividend is paid at a 102 percent payout, so all three engines must work at once and their joint odds are low. The competing hypothesis is the cleared branch of our own case, priced at its odds rather than adopted.

- At the 'Foundations': the foundations are eroding, not robust. The business foundations research's own aggregate finding is world-class capital returns alongside eroding network leadership, deteriorating satisfaction and rising churn, a structural contradiction; the risks research's winning profile is the false friend, the EBITDA margin held by cost cuts and possibly by under-investment (capex 12 percent of sales against peers' 18 percent) while the organic base decays; on that reading 'Business' is C and the Building Block D. Conceded: the network-quality evidence and the late-2025 churn and ARPU. Held at C because the outputs are still being generated (return on capital employed 17.70 percent; margin 36.5 percent; churn 16.7 percent), the risks research itself rates under-investment low plausibility, and the structure (three players following price rises by March 2026) is more robust than two quarters' behaviour. Would move to D on two more quarters of ARPU below EUR 24.0 with churn above 17 percent.
triggers: - 21-Oct-26 (Q3 2026): sequential mobile service revenue; churn below 17 percent and ARPU above EUR 24.0 confirm; still worsening sequentially, or ARPU below EUR 24.0 with churn above 17 percent, moves the turn to unlikely; Q3 comparable EBITDA below EUR 210 million is the alarm on the cost programme and on a further guidance cut.

- Q4 2026 print: mobile service revenue growth at +1.5 percent or better year on year confirms the case and moves the turn to likely; below +1.5 percent invalidates; FY2026 comparable EBITDA at EUR 830 million or better confirms, below EUR 815 million invalidates; comparable cash flow above EUR 100 million confirms, below EUR 80 million is the alarm; non-comparable adjustments above EUR 10 million a year refute; a cut to headline EBITDA guidance would convert the fit to 'Major CfC Clearing'.

- Q1 2027 and 2027: consumer postpaid ARPU above EUR 24.50 with two sequential rises confirms; below EUR 23.9 refutes; two consecutive quarters above EUR 24.50 raise the odds of growth rebuilding toward likely; churn above 20 percent refutes; two more quarters of ARPU below EUR 24.0 with churn above 17 percent move 'Business' to C and 'Foundations' to D.

- Software: organic growth above 8 percent in Q3 and Q4 2026 with positive segment EBITDA confirms; 0 to 2 percent refutes; two further quarters of negative segment EBITDA with guidance cut again invalidates the second engine.

- Dividend: a pause in growth is the alarm; a cut invalidates; FY2026 free cash flow before dividends below EUR 390 million invalidates cover; a freeze would take the yield floor to 12.7x and is the perception shock for an income register.

- Other alarms: 5G subscription penetration below 55 percent; capex to sales below 11.00 percent (under-investment); the multiple below 13.4x (the five-year low); a renewed campaign in the seasonally heavy H2 2026; Elisa last of three on Opensignal and EPSI again in 2026; renewed estimate cuts after the Q3 print.
